research_domain_title: Shared Prosperity Retirement, Social Security Floor, and Local Aging Networks
note: Major national doctrine. Do not replace Social Security first — transform it into the permanent guaranteed floor beneath a larger shared-wealth retirement system. Contribution formulas, trust sizes, and transition revenue require modeling. Legal drafting 0%. Architecture ≠ evidence that Citizen Ownership Accounts or Community Prosperity Trusts already exist.

public_promise.text: No earned Social Security benefit will be taken away. Current retirees and people nearing retirement remain fully protected. Constitutional Capitalism adds ownership, healthcare security, housing stability, transportation, energy affordability, and community dividends so retirement becomes a period of security and participation—not mere survival.

memorable_framing.protect_not_replace: We are protecting Social Security and building the retirement system that should always have existed above it.
memorable_framing.ownership_not_takeover: Every citizen will gain real ownership in the prosperity their work helped create.
memorable_framing.community_not_welfare: Communities will return part of their shared earnings to the people who built and sustained them.
memorable_framing.vision: Social Security keeps you from falling. Constitutional Capitalism helps you continue rising.

doctrine_statement.text: A lifetime of work, caregiving, military service, civic participation, entrepreneurship, and community contribution should produce more than subsistence in old age. The republic shall preserve a guaranteed foundation of retirement security while enabling every person to accumulate ownership, share in national productivity, participate in the prosperity of the community they helped build, and age with healthcare, housing, transportation, medicine, energy, dignity, and meaningful civic belonging.

items.text: SSA states that nearly 71 million Social Security beneficiaries will see the 2.8 percent COLA beginning in January 2026.

SSA’s Primary Insurance Amount formula applies progressive bend-point percentages (90%, 32%, and 15% for 2026 eligibility), so lower average indexed monthly earnings receive a higher replacement share than higher earnings.

The 2026 Social Security Trustees Report Summary projects that the OASI Trust Fund can pay 100% of scheduled benefits until the fourth quarter of 2032; thereafter continuing income would cover about 78% of scheduled benefits unless Congress acts.
GAO found that about one in ten low-income households approaching retirement (ages 51–64) had a retirement account balance in 2019, compared with about nine in ten high-income households.

IRS describes an ESOP as a qualified defined contribution plan that must be designed to invest primarily in qualifying employer securities — useful for employee ownership but requiring diversification safeguards for a national ownership account.

layers.title: Social Security Guarantee
layers.summary: Social Security remains the national guarantee against poverty, disability, premature death of a supporting worker, and extreme longevity. It is the security layer, not the entire retirement vision. Never convert entirely into private investment accounts.
provides: protections for caregivers and interrupted work histories
a stronger minimum benefit for people who worked or contributed over a lifetime
protection from market crashes and outliving personal savings
layers.financing_note: Stabilize transparently during transition. Options requiring modeling may include broadening the contribution base, shifting part of employer contribution into a corporate social-contribution system, and dedicating transition revenue from financial reform, energy returns, or reduced tax avoidance.

layers.title: National Citizen Ownership Account
layers.summary: Every person receives a portable account from adulthood—or potentially birth—that accumulates diversified ownership throughout life. Individually owned, portable, professionally managed, raid-protected, fee-protected, partially inheritable, partly convertible to lifetime income at retirement.
inflows: verified civic and military service credits
account_properties: converted partly into lifetime income at retirement

layers.title: Local Community Prosperity Accounts
layers.summary: People who live, work, raise families, volunteer, teach, farm, build businesses, serve in public institutions, or otherwise contribute gradually earn participation in a Community Prosperity Trust. Must not trap people geographically — benefits vest gradually and remain partially portable.
layers.community_principle: When a community grows wealth, the people who built and sustained that community should share in its enduring prosperity.
eligibility_builds_through: years of local work or business ownership
military service followed by community participation
documented periods of disability or family care

layers.title: Retirement Essentials
layers.summary: Retirement security cannot be measured only by a monthly check. The guarantee includes access to essential systems so aging is security and participation, not mere survival.

essentials.healthcare: Essential healthcare follows the person and is not dependent on former employment. Medicare becomes part of the universal health foundation.
essentials.housing: Secure aging in place — property-tax relief on protected primary residence, home repair and accessibility, multigenerational housing, community land trusts, reverse-mortgage protections, smaller community housing options, long-term care alternatives to institutional placement.
essentials.transportation: Community transit, demand-responsive rural transportation, medical transport, regional rail and bus, volunteer and cooperative driver networks. Loss of driving ability must not mean loss of citizenship or community participation.
essentials.medicine: Essential medicines affordable through public negotiation, generic competition, transparent pricing, and nonprofit or public production when markets fail.
essentials.energy: Protected block of essential household energy at lowest sustainable cost, supported by community-owned generation and the national energy-dividend system.
essentials.food_and_daily_services: Local food networks, meal delivery, community kitchens, home support, and preventive wellness.

local_aging_and_family_care.summary: Build Local Aging and Family Care Networks so families are not forced to choose only between unsupported home caregiving and expensive distant institutional placement.
local_aging_and_family_care.default_rule: Help people remain with family and community for as long as it is safe, desired, and medically appropriate.

corporate_responsibility.summary: Shift more retirement financing responsibility from taxes on individual labor toward institutions that benefit from that labor. Small businesses receive lower rates, simplified administration, or public matching — not crushed local employers.

thirty_year_transition.summary: Transition over roughly 30 years. Additions before replacements. Only after the new system is fully funded, independently audited, stress-tested through recessions, and shown to outperform the old structure should any payroll-financing mechanism be reduced or transferred.

eras.title: Protect and stabilize
actions: Legally guarantee all accrued and current Social Security benefits
Stabilize Social Security financing
Create legal framework for Citizen Ownership Accounts
Begin Community Prosperity Trust pilots
Consolidate retirement-account fees and improve portability
Build local aging-service networks
Begin housing, transportation, medicine, and energy protections
Publish individual transition statements

eras.title: Add ownership
actions: Require or phase in corporate prosperity contributions
Begin automatic citizen-account deposits
Stronger matches for low- and middle-income workers
Add military, caregiving, teaching, and civic-service credits
Expand employee ownership and diversified profit-sharing
Grow local community trusts
Pilot community retirement dividends

eras.title: Build local prosperity
actions: Community energy, resource, land, and enterprise returns produce meaningful local income
Retirement essentials increasingly shift from individual bills to community-supported services
Citizen accounts become large enough for supplemental retirement income
Long-term care moves toward local and home-based delivery
Property-tax reform improves permanent ownership security

rules: No current retiree receives less because of the transition.
Near-retirees remain under the system they planned around unless they voluntarily choose a demonstrably better option.
New ownership benefits are additions before they become replacements.
Retirement accounts cannot be raided for ordinary government spending.
Community funds cannot be controlled by political parties.
Private managers face strict fee and conflict rules.
Every person receives a plain-language annual statement.
Automatic correction mechanisms activate if funding falls below safe levels.

questions: Does the proposal protect all earned Social Security benefits for current and near-retirees?
Are new ownership layers additions before any replacement of the guarantee floor?
Does the Citizen Ownership Account diversify beyond single-employer stock?
Do Community Prosperity benefits vest through contribution without trapping people geographically?
Are healthcare, housing, transportation, medicine, energy, and food treated as retirement essentials?
Are family caregivers recognized with credits, continuity, and respite—not unpaid sacrifice alone?
Do large productive enterprises help finance the people and communities that make profits possible, without crushing small local employers?
Is the transition staged over decades with plain-language individual statements?
Do Retirement Security Covenant raid, fee, stress-test, and correction rules apply?
Would payroll-financing reductions wait until independent audit and recession stress tests confirm outperformance?
